claims.text: GDACS's Tropical Cyclone report for CHAMPI-26 (event id 1001338, episode 16, GLIDE TC-2026-000192-GUM) rates the storm an Overall Red alert (score 2.5), tracking Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands over a 14-18 October 2026 window, with an estimated 180,000 people exposed to Category 1 (120 km/h) or higher winds and a JTWC-sourced maximum sustained wind of 259 km/h. Vulnerability for Guam is rated medium.

GDACS's tropical cyclone report for CHAMPI-26 (event id 1001338, episode 46, GLIDE TC-2026-000192-GUM) now gives a tracking window of 14-25 October 2026, with peak intensity unchanged at 296 km/h (Category 5, JTWC) and the estimated population exposed to Category 1 or higher winds revised up to about 290,000, from about 180,000 in episode 35. Affected areas now additionally list China and South Korea, alongside the Philippines, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands and Japan. The report's mirrored media headlines (24-26 October) report about 56,000 households in Taiwan without electricity and separately describe damage in Taiwan and Okinawa with rainfall exceeding 200mm across Japan, noting the system weakened into an extratropical depression; GDACS's own casualty-estimate section remains empty and the report gives no death or injury figures.

NWS Tiyan Guam's active-alerts feed (api.weather.gov, checked 17 October 2026) lists a Typhoon Warning for Guam and Rota and a Typhoon Watch plus Tropical Storm Warning for Tinian and Saipan, issued 3:06 PM ChST: Typhoon Champi (29W) was about 225 miles east-southeast of Guam, moving west-northwest at 18 mph, forecast to pass just south of or over Guam as a Category 3 storm, likely Sunday morning. The feed also lists a Coastal Flood Warning and High Surf Warning (issued 4:31 PM ChST, surf to 35 feet on Guam, 20-25 feet on Rota, 15-20 feet on Tinian/Saipan, coastal inundation of 5-7 feet on Guam) and a Flood Watch (issued 4:10 PM ChST, forecast rainfall of 8-14 inches on Guam, 5-8 inches on Rota, 3-5 inches on Tinian/Saipan).

NWS Tiyan Guam's active-alerts feed (api.weather.gov, checked 18 October 2026, 7:05 PM ChST): a Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued 5:51 PM ChST states the Typhoon Warnings for Guam and Rota have been cancelled, instructing residents to stay in shelter until the all-clear. At the 5 PM ChST advisory, Typhoon Champi (29W) was centered near 13.0N 142.3E, about 170 miles west of Guam, moving west at 10 mph with maximum sustained winds near 150 mph (Super Typhoon strength), continuing to move away from Guam and the Marianas. Guam, Rota, Tinian and Saipan remain under a Wind Advisory (southeast winds 25-35 mph on Guam/Rota, 15-25 mph on Saipan/Tinian), a High Surf Advisory (9-14 ft surf) and Rip Current Statement, and a Flood Watch (forecast 1-4 inches of additional rain from outer rainbands), all through 4:00 AM ChST on 19 October. No deaths, injuries or damage have yet been confirmed by an authoritative source.

GDACS's tropical cyclone report for CHAMPI-26 (event id 1001338, episode 20, GLIDE TC-2026-000192-GUM), tracking window 14 Oct 2026 12:00 UTC to 19 Oct 2026 06:00 UTC, rates the storm an Overall Red alert (score 2.5) with a JTWC-sourced maximum sustained wind of 278 km/h (Category 5), up from 259 km/h in episode 16; estimated population exposed to Category 1 or higher winds is now about 230,000, up from 180,000, across Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands and Japan. Vulnerability for Guam remains rated medium.

NWS Tiyan Guam's active-alerts feed (api.weather.gov, checked 19 October 2026): Guam and Rota remain under a Rip Current Statement and a High Surf Advisory, both issued 3:55 PM ChST and valid until 4:00 AM ChST on 20 October, attributed to the remnant southerly swell of Super Typhoon Champi, which is slowly diminishing; surf may drop below the advisory threshold around 20 October, which would allow the alerts to expire. No damage reports are mentioned in the feed.

GDACS's tropical cyclone report for CHAMPI-26 (event id 1001338, episode 20) now gives a tracking window of 14-21 October 2026 and a JTWC-sourced peak intensity of 296 km/h (Category 5), up from the 278 km/h recorded on 19 October, with the estimated population exposed to Category 1 or higher winds unchanged at about 230,000 across Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands and Japan.

NWS Tiyan Guam's weather forecast office page (checked 21 October 2026, 7:06 PM ChST) states there are no watches, warnings, or advisories in effect for Guam, and no active tropical cyclones -- confirming the Rip Current Statement and High Surf Advisory tied to Champi's remnant swell have expired as forecast. No deaths, injuries or damage have been confirmed by an authoritative source for Guam or the Northern Mariana Islands.

GDACS's tropical cyclone report for CHAMPI-26 (event id 1001338, episode 32, GLIDE TC-2026-000192-GUM) now gives a tracking window of 14-22 October 2026, with peak intensity unchanged at 296 km/h (Category 5, JTWC) and population exposed to Category 1 or higher winds unchanged at about 230,000. The report now additionally lists the Philippines and Taiwan among affected areas, alongside Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands and Japan, and cites a media item reporting sea travel suspended in five Bicol provinces, Philippines, due to a gale warning. No casualty or damage figures are reported.

GDACS's tropical cyclone report for CHAMPI-26 (event id 1001338, episode 35, GLIDE TC-2026-000192-GUM) gives a tracking window of 14-23 October 2026, with peak intensity unchanged at 296 km/h (Category 5, JTWC) and the estimated population exposed to Category 1 or higher winds at about 180,000 (revised down from about 230,000 in episode 32). Affected areas are listed as the Philippines, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands and Japan -- Taiwan is no longer listed. The report cites no media item or casualty figure newer than the 21 October item on sea travel suspended in five Bicol provinces, Philippines, and the PAGER casualty section remains empty. Re-checked 24 October 2026: still the latest published episode (35), with the same window, intensity, exposed population and affected-areas list.

description: Typhoon Champi tracked through the western Pacific in October 2026, passing Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands before continuing past the Philippines toward Taiwan, Japan, China and South Korea. GDACS's latest tropical cyclone report (episode 46, window 14-25 October) rates the storm an Overall Red alert with a JTWC-sourced peak intensity of 296 km/h (Category 5) and an estimated 290,000 people exposed to Category 1 or higher winds, up from about 180,000 as its track widened. The storm passed about 170 miles west of Guam on 18 October without a direct landfall there; GDACS's mirrored media headlines report roughly 56,000 households left without power in Taiwan and further damage in Taiwan and Okinawa with heavy rain over Japan, before the system weakened into an extratropical depression. GDACS's own report gives no confirmed death or injury figures.

GDACS's mirrored media headlines report roughly 56,000 households left without electricity in Taiwan and damage in Taiwan and Okinawa with rainfall exceeding 200mm across Japan, before the system weakened into an extratropical depression. GDACS's own casualty-estimate section remains empty and gives no confirmed death or injury figures for the storm.

name: Typhoon Champi — Guam & Northern Mariana Islands

updates.text: GDACS extended the tracking window to 14-25 October (episode 46) as Champi's track widened to include China and South Korea; exposed population rose to ~290,000 (from ~180,000). Media mirrored on GDACS report ~56,000 Taiwan households without power and Taiwan/Okinawa damage with heavy Japan rain, before the storm weakened to an extratropical depression. No confirmed deaths/injuries.

GDACS extended the tracking window to 14-23 October (episode 35) and revised the exposed-population estimate down to about 180,000 (from ~230,000); Taiwan no longer appears on the affected-areas list, which now reads Philippines, Guam, Northern Mariana Islands and Japan. Peak intensity (296 km/h) is unchanged; no deaths or damage confirmed.

GDACS extended the tracking window to 14-22 October (episode 32) as Champi continued toward Okinawa's Sakishima Islands and Taiwan, now also listing the Philippines among affected areas after a gale warning suspended sea travel in five Bicol provinces. Peak intensity (296 km/h) and exposed population (~230,000) are unchanged; no deaths or damage confirmed.

GDACS revised Champi's peak intensity up to 296 km/h (Category 5, JTWC) and extended its tracking window to 14-21 October; NWS Tiyan Guam reports no watches, warnings or advisories remain in effect for Guam, confirming the storm's remnant-swell advisories have expired as forecast. The storm continues toward waters south of Okinawa, Japan.

GDACS's latest report (episode 20) raised Champi's peak intensity to 278 km/h (Category 5, JTWC) and exposed population to about 230,000 across Guam, the Marianas and Japan, up from 259 km/h and 180,000. Only a Rip Current Statement and High Surf Advisory persist from the storm's diminishing swell, expected to expire around 20 October. No deaths or damage confirmed.

Champi reached Super Typhoon strength (259 km/h sustained winds) and passed about 170 miles west of Guam without a direct landfall; NWS cancelled its Typhoon Warnings for Guam and Rota the evening of 18 October as the storm moved away west. A Wind Advisory, High Surf Advisory and Flood Watch remain active into 19 October. No deaths or damage confirmed yet.
